excerpts: **GPU Partitioning (GPU-P)** is a feature in Windows Server 2025 Hyper-V that allows multiple virtual machines to share a single physical GPU by dividing it into isolated fractions. Each VM is allocated a dedicated portion of the GPU’s resources (memory, compute, encoders, etc.) instead of using the entire GPU. This is achieved via **Single-Root I/O Virtualization (SR-IOV)** , which provides a hardware-enforced isolation between GPU partitions, ensuring each VM can access only its assigned GPU fraction with predictable performance and security.

Each VM is allocated a dedicated portion of the GPU’s resources (memory, compute, encoders, etc.) instead of using the entire GPU. This is achieved via **Single-Root I/O Virtualization (SR-IOV)** , which provides a hardware-enforced isolation between GPU partitions, ensuring each VM can access only its assigned GPU fraction with predictable performance and security.

In contrast, **GPU Passthrough** (also known as Discrete Device Assignment, _DDA_ ) assigns a whole physical GPU exclusively to one VM. With DDA, the VM gets full control of the GPU, but no other VMs can use that GPU simultaneously. GPU-P’s ability to time-slice or partition the GPU allows higher utilization and VM density for graphics or compute workloads, whereas DDA offers maximum performance for a single VM at the cost of flexibility.

GPU-P is ideal when you want to share a GPU among multiple VMs, such as for VDI desktops or AI inference tasks that only need a portion of a GPU’s power. DDA (passthrough) is preferred when a workload needs the full GPU (e.g. large model training) or when the GPU doesn’t support partitioning.

GPU Partitioning in Windows Server 2025 is supported on select GPU hardware that provides SR-IOV or similar virtualization capabilities, along with appropriate drivers. Only specific GPUs support GPU-P and you won’t be able to configure it on a consumer gaming GPU like your RTX 5090. In addition to the GPU itself, certain platform features are required: **Modern CPU with IOMMU:** The host processors must support Intel VT-d or AMD-Vi with DMA remapping (IOMMU). This is crucial for mapping device memory securely between host and VMs. Older processors lacking these enhancements may not fully support live migration of GPU partitions. **BIOS Settings:** Ensure that in each host’s UEFI/BIOS, Intel VT-d/AMD-Vi and SR-IOV are enabled. These options may be under virtualization or PCIe settings. Without SR-IOV enabled at the firmware level, the OS will not recognize the GPU as partitionable (in Windows Admin Center it might show status “Paravirtualization” indicating the driver is capable but the platform isn’t).

Do you have questions about our pricing? Frequently asked questions How are your services billed? UpCloud uses a prepaid system where you can add balance to your account by making a payment at any time. Your services are then deducted from this balance on an hourly basis. Can I pay in other currencies than EUR? Yes, you can pay in other currencies other than EUR. We support payments made in EUR, USD, GBP, and SGP. Payments that are not in EUR will be exchanged to EUR. The day’s exchange rate, which is the market rate of the currency, will be applied. You can find the exchange rate in your UpCloud Control Panel when making a payment. How can I stop the charges to my account? You are able to delete the services at any point. The service charge accumulation will stop the point of deletion. You will be able to utilise your remaining balance at any time. Which regions can I deploy in? UpCloud runs 15 data centres across the globe, so you can put your infrastructure close to your users for lower latency, or in a specific region to keep your data where you need it. For more information see our [Data Centers page](https://upcloud.com/data-centers/) . Are there any hidden fees? No, and we’re a bit proud of that. The price you see is the price you pay, aside from any local taxes that apply where you are. No egress charges, no surprise line items, no penalty for leaving. Everything’s laid out on this page, and if anything’s unclear our [sales team](https://upcloud.com/contact/) is happy to walk you through it. Can I try before I buy, without signing up? Yes, if you’d rather not create an account yet. Our [live demo](http://demo.upcloud.com/?currency=EUR) lets you explore the UpCloud platform with no signup and no commitment. Kick the tyres, then sign up when you’re ready. Is there a free trial? Yes. New sign-ups get free credit to try UpCloud before committing to a paid plan. The exact amount changes from time to time, so head to the [sign-up page](https://signup.upcloud.com/?promo=boost500) to see the current offer. What does zero-cost data transfer actually mean? It means outbound data transfer is free, full stop. Most providers quietly add egress fees that swell your bill as your traffic grows. We don’t. Both inbound and outbound transfer are included at no extra cost on every plan, with our [Fair Transfer Policy](https://upcloud.com/fair-transfer-policy) keeping things sensible. There’s more on this over on the [Zero-cost Egress page](https://upcloud.com/products/zero-cost-egress/) . Are all your products covered by the zero-cost egress policy? Our [zero-cost egress policy](https://upcloud.com/products/zero-cost-egress/) applies exclusively to standard traffic originating directly from UpCloud data centers. Content delivery network traffic processed through our CDN powered by [bunny.net](http://bunny.net/) operates under a separate billing model and is excluded from this [zero-cost egress policy](https://upcloud.com/products/zero-cost-egress/) . Do you offer refunds? We offer a 30-day money back guarantee during which you can have a full refund on your first payment. We are unable to offer refunds on unused balance outside this period. Need help planning your infrastructure? We’ve got you covered! [Contact our sales team](https://upcloud.com/contact/) You're viewing the EU site.
